questions.question: What was the immediate cause of Coonan cross Oath and its after effects?
questions.solution_html:
• Coonan Cross Oath (1653)
  • The Coonan cross oath on 3rd January 1653 is the historic revolt of the St.
  • Thomas Christmas against the imposition of Latin rule.
  • This was the culmination of the general unrest felt among the St. Thomas
  • Christians due to the enforced decisions of the Synod of Diamper.
  • The Malabar Christians became enraged and assembled before a cross at
  • Mattancherry near Cochin on January 3rd 1653 and holding a rope tied to the
  • cross swear that they
  • would no more be subordinate to the Latin rule in Church life.
  • This event 1653 broke the 50 years old Roman supremacy imposed at the Synod
  • of Diamper in 1599.

questions.question: Write notes on life and works of St. Ephrem.
questions.solution_html:
• ST. EPHREM
  • St. Ephrem is the greatest Syriac writer whose contributions are unique in the
  • fields of poetry, theology and Biblical interpretations. He is one of the most
  • prominent fathers and doctors of the universal Christian Church. He was born at
  • Nisibis in the Roman Empire about 306 AD. t. Ephrem grew as a brilliant
  • scholar and learned theologian. When St. Jacob went to Nicaea to take part in
  • the Ecumenical council of AD 325, Ephrem also accompanied him. Ephrem
  • played a significant role in refuting the heretical views of Arius in the council.
